title: Malaise
hpi_narrative: {{patient_name}} presents with vague abdominal/pelvic discomfort, early satiety, bloating, increased abdominal girth, urinary frequency, and unintentional weight loss — classic insidious presentation of ovarian cancer. Exam may reveal pelvic mass, ascites, omental cake. Ovarian cancer is the leading cause of gynecologic cancer death because it presents late. Workup: transvaginal ultrasound (first-line imaging — adnexal mass, complex cystic-solid, ascites), CA-125 tumor marker (elevated in 80% of advanced ovarian cancer, but not diagnostic — also elevated in endometriosis, PID, fibroids), CT abdomen/pelvis for staging. Definitive diagnosis: surgical exploration with staging laparotomy (TAH-BSO, omentectomy, lymph node sampling). Refer to gynecologic oncology. BRCA testing if family history (germline BRCA1/2 in ~15%).
chief_complaint: Abdominal bloating, early satiety, weight loss, pelvic discomfort
